module purpose: neorv32_trng turns bus writes into an enable bit and a one-cycle pool-clear request, runs the neoTRNG entropy source (per-cell oscillator loops whose synchronized outputs are XOR-combined, accepted pairwise and shifted into a byte with a completion count), writes each finished byte into a FIFO sub-unit that is not supplied, and on bus reads returns either a status word or a byte popped from that FIFO.

use-case flows.value: enable setting taken from bus write data bit ctrl_en_c and held in enable
enable propagated into the entropy source: copied to sample_en, chained through each cell's enable shift register, releasing the inverter stages and the pairing phase
raw entropy bit of each cell: oscillator latch loop, two-stage synchronization and cell output
cell outputs XOR-combined, accepted pairwise and shifted into a byte, with a count of accepted bits that signals a finished byte
finished byte and its write strobe handed to the random-pool FIFO sub-unit
pool byte returned on a read with addr(2) = '1' (zero when the pool reports nothing available), with the pool read strobe
status word: enable, FIFO size constant, simulation-mode constant and pool availability
random-pool clear while enable is '0' or on the one-cycle fifo_clr request
rstn_i low clears enable, fifo_clr, the bus response, the pairing and sampling registers, the cell enable shift registers and the synchronizers

conceptual assets.concept: Entropy-source enable setting -- whether the entropy cells run, sampling proceeds and the random pool is kept
conceptual assets.reasoning: Configure flow: under bus_req_i.stb = '1' and bus_req_i.rw = '1' (lines 103-104), `enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` (line 105) holds the setting. Its effects: enable = '0' asserts fifo.clear (line 170); enable is wired to neoTRNG_inst.enable_i (line 137) and copied to sample_en (line 354), which zeroes sample_cnt and sample_sreg while '0' (lines 355-357) and drives cell_en_in(0) (line 311). In each cell, en_i forces latch to '0' when '0' (line 435) and is shifted into sreg (line 416). The bits of sreg release the inverter stages one at a time (line 435), and its top bit leaves as en_o (line 421) to enable the next cell (line 312) and to let debias_state toggle (line 336). Integrity: the held setting and every gating effect above must follow the last write. Availability is also Established: random bytes are produced only while this enable reaches the cells and the sampler (lines 336, 355-360). enable stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3; it GATES fifo.clear and connects to neoTRNG_inst.enable_i). enable_i sets (CARRIES sample_en, line 354). sample_en stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4; GATES sample_cnt and sample_sreg at line 355); it copies an input port, so the copy rule does not remove it. en_i sets (GATES latch, line 435). sreg stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, line 416; GATES latch at line 435 and SOURCES the output port en_o). en_o is an exit port (DERIVES_FROM sreg, line 421). Not listed: bus_req_i is a transport record (addr, data, ben, stb, rw), so it is no setting point, and the readback through bus_rsp_o.data (line 109) is a transport exit; cell_en_in(0) COPIES sample_en (line 311), so it is a copy; cell_en_out only forwards en_o (line 312) and gates debias_state (line 336). No line restricts reading the setting (line 109), so confidentiality is not established. The MAP CHECK lists the CLOCKED_BY and RESET_BY records of enable and sample_en as lacking a partner, but clk_i and rstn_i of each entity carry SEQUENCES and RESETS records naming them (lines 92, 96, 349, 353).

conceptual assets.concept: Random-pool clear decision -- whether the FIFO of random bytes is told to clear (while disabled or on a clear request)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Reset flow: a write sets `fifo_clr <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_fifo_clr_c);` (line 106), and line 101 returns it to '0' on every other clock edge, so it holds a one-cycle clear request. `fifo.clear <= '1' when (enable = '0') or (fifo_clr = '1') else '0';` (line 170) computes the clear decision, and line 157 wires it to rnd_pool_fifo_inst.clear_i. The FIFO entity is not supplied, so under the integrator assumption Integrity is Established: the FIFO must receive exactly the decision of line 170. What the FIFO does on a clear is not visible here, so no availability claim is made. fifo_clr stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4; GATES fifo.clear at line 170). fifo.clear computes (GATED_BY fifo_clr, occurrence 3); it is an internal record field computed here from a decision, so the sub-unit wiring exception holds. enable is an operand of this decision and is listed under the enable concept, not here. The request arrives on bus_req_i.data, a field of a transport record, so no port is listed as its setting point.

conceptual assets.concept: Raw entropy bit of each entropy cell -- the free-running oscillator value, synchronized and output by the cell
conceptual assets.reasoning: Operate flow in neoTRNG_cell: `latch(i) <= '0' when (en_i = '0') else latch(i) when (sreg(i) = '0') else inv_out(i);` (line 435), with inv_in taking the latch outputs rotated by one stage (lines 457-458) and inv_out inverting inv_in (line 440, or a clocked inversion at line 449 when the generic SIM_MODE is true), forms a closed inversion loop. `sync <= sync(0) & latch(latch'left);` (line 470) captures it over two clock edges and `rnd_o <= sync(1);` (line 475) outputs it. neoTRNG uses it: cell_rnd is XOR-combined into cell_sum (lines 320-322), shifted into debias_sreg (line 334), and feeds the acceptance test (line 341) and the sampled byte (line 360). Integrity: the sampled byte is defined from these cell outputs (lines 320, 334, 342, 360). Availability is also Established: if the synchronized outputs stop changing, debias_sreg(1) xor debias_sreg(0) stays '0', debias_valid never asserts (line 341), sample_cnt never advances (line 359) and valid_o (line 367) never signals a byte. latch computes (DERIVES_FROM inv_out, occurrence 2; it is also GATED_BY en_i and sreg there). sync stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3; SOURCES the output port rnd_o); it names both latch and itself, so it is not a copy. rnd_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM sync, line 475). Not listed: inv_in only routes latch outputs and inv_out only inverts them inside the loop; cell_rnd carries rnd_o into the combination of neoTRNG (line 306) and is a partner, not a further reference; cell_sum, debias_sreg and debias_data are steps of the computation whose result sample_sreg stores, and the records of debias_sreg show only data passed to internal elements. No line establishes a confidentiality property.

conceptual assets.concept: Sampled random byte -- the byte assembled from accepted bits and handed to the random pool
conceptual assets.reasoning: Operate flow in neoTRNG: when sampling is active and debias_valid = '1' (lines 355, 358), `sample_sreg <= sample_sreg(6 downto 0) & (sample_sreg(7) xor debias_data);` (line 360) shifts an accepted bit in; the register is zeroed when sample_en = '0' or the byte is complete (lines 355-357). `data_o <= sample_sreg;` (line 366) drives it out, and in neorv32_trng it reaches rnd_pool_fifo_inst.wdata_i through fifo.wdata (lines 139, 161). The FIFO is not supplied, so under the integrator assumption Integrity is Established: the pool must receive exactly the byte defined by lines 360 and 366. sample_sreg stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4; CARRIES the output port data_o). data_o is the exit port (COPIES sample_sreg, line 366). Not listed: fifo.wdata only receives data_o and passes it unchanged to wdata_i, and fifo.rdata only receives rdata_o and is read as data into the response (line 117), so both are carriers; bus_rsp_o is a transport record. The read-out of the byte to the requester therefore has no eligible reference inside neorv32_trng. Any qualified read returns the byte (lines 113-117) and no line restricts it, so confidentiality is context-dependent and not claimed.

conceptual assets.concept: Bit acceptance decision -- whether the current pair of combined bits is accepted into the sample, with the pairing phase it depends on
conceptual assets.reasoning: Operate flow: `debias_state <= (not debias_state) and cell_en_out(cell_en_out'left);` (line 336) alternates the pairing phase while the last cell is enabled, and `debias_valid <= debias_state and (debias_sreg(1) xor debias_sreg(0));` (line 341) accepts a pair only in that phase and only when its two bits differ. debias_valid gates the shift of sample_sreg and the count in sample_cnt (lines 358-360). Integrity: a wrong decision shifts unaccepted bits into the byte and miscounts its completion. Availability is also Established: without this decision no bit is sampled and no byte completes (lines 358-359, 367). debias_valid computes (GATED_BY debias_state, occurrence 2). debias_state stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3; GATES debias_valid at line 341): its own value is the phase state the decision depends on. Not listed: debias_sreg feeds the decision only as data (SOURCES debias_valid), and cell_en_out only forwards en_o and gates debias_state.

conceptual assets.concept: Byte-complete event -- the count of accepted bits and the valid strobe that writes a finished byte into the pool
conceptual assets.reasoning: Operate flow: `sample_cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(sample_cnt) + 1);` (line 359) counts accepted bits; when its top bit is set, line 355 zeroes the count and the sample register (lines 356-357), and `valid_o <= sample_cnt(sample_cnt'left);` (line 367) signals a finished byte. In neorv32_trng valid_o drives fifo.we (line 138), wired to rnd_pool_fifo_inst.we_i (line 162). The FIFO is not supplied, so Integrity is Established under the integrator assumption: the pool must receive exactly the write strobe of line 367, raised only after the counted accepted bits. Availability is also Established: random bytes enter the pool only through this strobe (lines 138, 162). sample_cnt stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 6; SOURCES the output port valid_o and GATES sample_sreg at line 355); the flow graph lists it as self-updating. valid_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM sample_cnt, line 367). Not listed: fifo.we only receives valid_o and passes it unchanged to we_i, and no condition in this block tests it, so it is a carrier.

conceptual assets.concept: Random-pool read decision -- whether a bus access pops a byte from the pool
conceptual assets.reasoning: Read-out flow: `fifo.re <= '1' when (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.rw = '0') and (bus_req_i.addr(2) = '1') else '0';` (line 171) decides whether the access reads the pool, and line 165 wires it to rnd_pool_fifo_inst.re_i. The FIFO is not supplied, so Integrity is Established under the integrator assumption: the pool must receive exactly the decision of line 171. fifo.re computes (GATED_BY bus_req_i.stb, occurrence 3); it is an internal record field computed here from a decision, so the sub-unit wiring exception holds. Its operands are fields of bus_req_i, a transport record, so no input is listed as its setting point.

conceptual assets.concept: Random-pool availability status -- whether a buffered random byte may be returned to a reader
conceptual assets.reasoning: Read-out and report flows: fifo.avail is driven by rnd_pool_fifo_inst.avail_o (line 167) and tested in `if (fifo.avail = '0') then` (line 114): when '0' the read returns zeros (line 115), otherwise fifo.rdata (line 117); line 112 also reports it in the status word. Integrity: the read-out must return a pool byte only when this status says one is available, and the reported status must match it. fifo.avail sets: the CONNECTS edge of mode out (occurrence 4) brings the status of the sub-unit into this entity, and the field is tested in an if condition (line 114), which satisfies the sub-unit wiring exception; testing alone does not make it compute the test. Its exits are bits of bus_rsp_o.data, a field of a transport record, so no exit port is listed.
